issues.title: Stream as a control plane for RPC-over-QUIC
issues.author: chucklever
issues.body:
Section 3.3 (QUIC Streams) notes that QUIC's stream abstraction creates an opportunity to designate one stream as a control plane carrying out-of-band management messages rather than RPC traffic. The spec does not currently use this capability. This issue captures whether a control-plane stream should be defined, what messages it would carry, and how peers would discover one.

*Origin: aside in §3.3 of draft-cel-nfsv4-rpc-over-quicv1; raised by Chuck Lever.*

issues.title: Should each stream carry only one RPC program/version combination?
issues.author: chucklever
issues.body:
Section 3.3 leaves open whether a single QUIC stream may carry multiple RPC program/version combinations or whether each stream is restricted to one. Restricting to one would delegate program/version demultiplexing of ingress traffic to the QUIC layer (for example, NFSACL and NFS would each require their own stream). This issue captures the tradeoff and the decision.

*Origin: aside in §3.3 of draft-cel-nfsv4-rpc-over-quicv1; raised by Chuck Lever.*

issues.title: Stream lifecycle: reconnection, resend semantics, and stream reuse
issues.author: chucklever
issues.body:
Section 3.4 (RPC Message Framing) describes RPC record framing but leaves several stream-lifecycle questions unsettled:

1. QUIC permits reconnecting with the same connection ID and connection migration across paths. When may a server drop an in-flight request and when may a client resend? Is any advice needed for server-side DRC implementations? (Lars: which of connection migration, 0-RTT repeated connection, or something else is meant by "reconnecting"?)
2. Are callers expected to open a fresh stream per RPC, or to reuse one stream for a series of RPCs? Should the spec require one of these patterns?

*Origin: aside in §3.4 of draft-cel-nfsv4-rpc-over-quicv1; opening question carried over from the pre-2021 source (original raiser not recorded); follow-up clarifications by Lars Eggert.*

issues.title: Server backpressure mechanism for RPC-over-QUIC
issues.author: chucklever
issues.body:
RPC-over-QUIC needs a flow-control / backpressure mechanism analogous to the TCP receive window so that responders can signal when they cannot accept additional load. SERVER_BUSY (defined in §3.5) provides a coarse "no more right now" signal but is not a window-like mechanism. This issue captures whether a window-like mechanism is required and, if so, how it is conveyed.

*Origin: aside in §3.4 of draft-cel-nfsv4-rpc-over-quicv1; raised by Chuck Lever.*

issues.title: Why register a netid per IP address family?
issues.author: chucklever
issues.body:
Section 7.1 requests two netids ("quic" for IPv4, "quic6" for IPv6). This follows existing netid practice but appears to be a layering violation: the netid encodes both transport and address family. Is the per-AF split justified for RPC-over-QUIC, or should a single netid be used and the address family conveyed separately?

*Origin: aside in §7.1 of draft-cel-nfsv4-rpc-over-quicv1; raised by Lars Eggert (with response by Chuck Lever noting that netids are arguably technical debt at this point).*

issues.title: Versioning of the RPC-over-QUIC ALPN identifier
issues.author: chucklever
issues.body:
Section 7.2 reuses the "sunrpc" ALPN string from RFC 9289 for RPC-over-QUIC. If future revisions of the RPC-over-QUIC binding need to be distinguished on the wire, how would that be negotiated? Should the binding use a versioned ALPN identifier rather than reusing the unversioned RFC 9289 string?

*Origin: aside in §7.2 of draft-cel-nfsv4-rpc-over-quicv1; raised by Lars Eggert.*

reviews.author: chucklever
reviews.body:
Thanks for your review and the PR!

I'd like to document the purpose for several of these changes in the document's commit history, and also request some changes to particular edits. Please split this commit into several smaller ones:
- One that moves the Reference for RFC7942, with a rationale in the patch description
- One that removes format="default" sectionFormat="of" from <xref> tags, with rationale
- One that changes the term "QUICv1" to "QUIC", with rationale
- One that changes the introduction to the Transport Layer Security section, with rationale
- One that applies the wordsmithing changes (rationale obvious)
- One that adds your asides and questions

If there's a friendly way via the GitHub BUI for me to split up this one commit to save you the effort, let me know how to do that, and give me rough suggestions for the rationale for each.
